Cullimore, Lincoln Fillmore, Keith Grover, Wayne A. Harper, David P. Hinkins, Don L. Ipson, John D. Johnson, Michael S. Kennedy, Daniel McCay, Michael K. McKell, Ann Millner, Derrin R. No votes (6): Nate Blouin, Luz Escamilla, Karen Kwan, Stephanie Pitcher, Jennifer Plumb, Kathleen A. Riebe.

HB467 is a Utah state measure that restricts abortion clinic operations. According to the Freedom Index, it 'Prevents an abortion clinic from being licensed after May 2, 2023, and from operating on or after January 1, 2024, or when their license expires.' The Utah Senate passed the bill on March 2, 2023, with a vote of 22 in favor and 6 opposed, with 1 legislator recording no vote.

HB467 would ban elective abortion clinics after May 2, requiring abortions to be performed in hospitals instead. It removes the rape and incest exemption for abortions after 18 weeks of pregnancy, and creates a legal presumption that girls under 14 who seek abortions are victims of rape or incest. The Legislature on Thursday approved the bill. The Republican-controlled Senate voted down all proposals from Democrats.

SB174 Conscience Exemptions for Health Providers, 3/2/2026, Passed 22-7, Lincoln Fillmore voted Yes. Under the bill, providers can only object to forms of treatment, rather than individual patients. The bill requires providers to notify Utah's Department of Health and Human Services when they object to a type of treatment, and post a prominent, visible sign in their office noting the objection.

SB16 Ban on Sex Mutilation Against Minors, 1/27/2023, Passed 20-8, Lincoln Fillmore voted Yes. SB16 would ban transgender surgeries for Utah children and teens and place an indefinite moratorium on puberty blockers and cross-sex hormones for minors.

The Utah Senate passed SB16 with a vote of 20-8. Two Republicans, Sen. David Hinkins, R-Ferron, and Sen. Todd Weiler, R-Woods Cross, joined Democrats in voting against the bill. SB16 would ban sex characteristic reassignment surgeries for Utahns under age 18 and impose an indefinite moratorium on hormonal treatments for Utah children and teens not already being treated for gender dysphoria for at least six months.

Legislature Overrides Veto on H.B. 11. The Senate voted 21-8 in favor of overriding the governor's veto. H.B. 11, titled 'Student Eligibility in Interscholastic Activities,' established restrictions on transgender participation in school sports. Sen. Lincoln Fillmore, Mike Kennedy, Mike McKell, Ann Millner and Senate Majority Leader Evan Vickers flipped to a 'yea' vote to secure the veto override on HB11 in March 2022.

HB300 Election Integrity, 3/6/2025, Passed 19-10, Lincoln Fillmore voted Yes. HB300 requires Utah voters to write the last four digits of their government-issued identification card on their ballot's return envelope. The bill phases out automatic mail-in ballots beginning January 1, 2028, requiring voters to opt in.

Utah lawmakers move forward with reforms to mail-in ballots. HB300 would require ballots to be in clerks' possession no later than 8 p.m. on election night, regardless of their postmark. The bill enhances the lieutenant governor's ability to investigate voter registration roll inaccuracies. The House voted 56-15 and the Senate voted 19-10 to approve the bill.

Sen. Lincoln Fillmore argued on the Senate floor: 'We need to ask ourselves a slightly different question. Instead of, what can we do to provide an education for 700,000 kids in this state? We need to ask ourselves, what can we do to provide the education we can for this child? And that is a difficult question to ask because it requires 700,000 answers.' The Senate voted 20-8 to approve HB215, creating the Utah Fits All Scholarship program.

HB215 creates the Utah Fits All Scholarship program, providing $8,000 scholarships to qualifying families for private school tuition and education expenses. The bill also allocates $196.9 million for a $6,000 pay raise for licensed educators. The Utah Senate approved HB215 with a vote of 20-8, passing by a two-thirds margin in both legislative chambers, which prevents referendum challenges.

Also voted No on SB258 State-Sponsored Preschool for All (2023) and No on HB100 Free School Meals (2025).

HB165 Illegal Immigration, 2/26/2024, Passed 63-11, Lincoln Fillmore voted Yes. SB217 CHIP 'Benefits' for Illegal Aliens, 3/2/2023, Passed 25-3, Lincoln Fillmore voted No. The No vote on SB217 reflects opposition to extending health benefits to non-citizen children; Yes on HB165 requires ICE to notify Utah three days before releasing undocumented immigrants in the state.

Cox signed the bill: 'We passed another bill to show that we're not a sanctuary state that requires ICE to communicate with us if they're going to release someone in the state who is undocumented, who is not here legally.'

Fillmore sponsored SB37 to redirect $842 million in school property tax revenue into the general fund to create more budget flexibility.

Sen. Lincoln Fillmore, R-South Jordan, was picked to serve on the 2025 Legislative Redistricting Committee. In 2021, Fillmore served on the Legislative Redistricting Committee that rejected all independent commission maps and passed legislature-drawn maps. A judge later ruled that the Legislature 'unconstitutionally repealed Proposition 4, and enacted SB 200, in violation of the people's fundamental right to reform redistricting in Utah and to prohibit partisan gerrymandering.'

Under SB200, which rolled back the 2018 Better Boundaries initiative, the Legislature retains final control over redistricting, as it is not bound to the maps proposed by the advisory commission. Senate Bill 200 was passed by the legislature on March 18, 2020, by a vote of 25-0 in the Senate and 67-4 in the House. In the 2020 cycle, the state's advisory independent commission proposed three each of congressional and state legislative maps — but the legislature ignored each.
